This addresses the retained prior finding and the author's correction comment. The configuration owner still assigns the fixed default.
Existing startup owner retained: The existing readiness loop consumes the increased timeout, verifies the spawned PID owns the endpoint, checks cancellation before adoption, and cleans up on failure. Remote and attach-only profiles take separate paths. The diff adds no authority-bearing value, public API, persisted setting, dependency, or security-policy change.
Regression coverage and proof scope: The added test exercises ensureBrowserAvailable with simulated 750 ms readiness responses and asserts that the launched browser remains registered without cleanup. Existing sibling tests cover failed readiness, foreign endpoint ownership, cancellation, and remote profiles. The complete supplied PR body reports 60 focused tests passing and expressly disclaims a live overloaded-Gateway reproduction; tests were not executed during this read-only review. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The browser plugin launches managed Chrome and checks its Chrome DevTools Protocol connection before reporting startup success. Failed readiness or ownership checks trigger cleanup of the launched process. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Browser start request] --> B[Launch managed Chrome] B --> C[Retry readiness probes] C --> D{Ready and owned?} D -->|Yes| E[Keep browser running] D -->|Timeout or failure| F[Clean up launched browser] ``` ## Before merge None.

The regression models that path; no live Gateway reproduction was performed. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes.
